A review of the beneficial ownership certification form provided at account opening identified Solveig Cromwell and Delia Dalrymple as holding equity interests of twenty-five percent and forty percent, respectively, with Thaddeus Fontaine listed as holding the remaining thirty-five percent and acting as the control person. The beneficial ownership certification was signed and dated by Thaddeus Fontaine on September 19, 2023, which was five days after the account was opened and, significantly, after the initial funding of the account had occurred. This sequence of events represents a departure from standard onboarding procedures, which require the beneficial ownership form to be executed prior to the activation of the account and the receipt of funds.

The file review further identified that the account was opened under a documentary exception. The exception was granted by the onboarding manager to permit the delayed collection of a valid government-issued identification document for Delia Dalrymple. The exception log indicated that a non-expired passport or driver's license was to be provided within thirty days of account opening. A review of the document repository confirmed that no such identification was ever received for Delia Dalrymple, and the documentary exception remained outstanding and uncleared at the time of this review. The only identification on file for Delia Dalrymple was an expired driver's license, which was submitted with the initial application package and was the basis for the exception request. Identification documents for Thaddeus Fontaine and Solveig Cromwell were present in the file and appeared to be current and valid at the time of onboarding. The failure to clear the documentary exception for a beneficial owner holding a forty percent stake represents a material deficiency in the customer identification program.

The customer profile section of the due diligence file contained limited information regarding the nature of the business and the expected account activity. The business description provided by Thaddeus Fontaine described Summit Gate Fabrication Inc. as a domestic supplier of fabricated metal components for the industrial machinery sector. The anticipated activity profile projected a transaction volume of several hundred thousand dollars per month, primarily consisting of domestic wire transfers and automated clearing house payments related to the purchase of raw materials and the sale of finished goods. The profile indicated that the primary counterparties would be domestic manufacturing and logistics firms. The expected source of initial funding was stated to be a transfer from an existing business account at another financial institution. The customer profile did not anticipate international wire activity or transactions involving entities outside of the fabrication and industrial machinery sectors. The occupation field for the control person, Thaddeus Fontaine, was left blank on the customer profile form, which is notable given the medium risk rating assigned to the entity.

An examination of the source of funds and source of wealth evidence in the file revealed significant gaps. The initial funding of the account occurred on September 15, 2023, via an incoming wire transfer in the amount of $872,548.20. The originator of this transfer was an entity named Mapleford Fabrication Holdings Ltd., which was not listed as an expected counterparty in the initial customer profile. The file did not contain any documentation, such as invoices, contracts, or loan agreements, to substantiate the business purpose of this transfer or the relationship between Summit Gate Fabrication Inc. and Mapleford Fabrication Holdings Ltd. The relationship manager did not document any inquiries made regarding this initial funding event. The lack of verified source of funds documentation for a transfer of this magnitude, particularly when originating from an unexpected third party, is a critical deficiency.

Subsequent to the initial funding, the account exhibited a pattern of activity that deviated significantly from the expected profile documented at onboarding. The file review identified that the largest single transaction conducted through the account was an outgoing wire transfer of $704,962.00, which occurred on October 18, 2023. This transfer was directed to Silverthorn Holdings Trading Co., an entity not previously identified as a supplier or customer. The transaction narrative indicated that the transfer was for consulting services. A review of the file found no evidence of a consulting agreement, invoices, or other documentation to support the legitimacy of this transaction or the business rationale for engaging consulting services of this value. The absence of source of funds evidence for this transaction further compromised the integrity of the due diligence file.

The aggregate activity conducted through the account during the review period totaled $2,885,112.91. This volume significantly exceeded the anticipated activity levels projected at onboarding. The transaction analysis indicated that a substantial portion of this activity involved counterparties that did not appear to align with the stated business purpose of Summit Gate Fabrication Inc. For example, the account received multiple incoming transfers from Summit Gate Trading Enterprises LLC and Lakebridge Exports Inc., entities whose names suggest trading and export activities rather than domestic manufacturing. The account also originated frequent payments to Obsidian Logistics Group LLC and Millpond Capital Holdings Ltd. The file did not contain any updated customer profile information or notes from the relationship manager explaining the shift in the transaction profile or the nature of the relationships with these newly identified counterparties. The declared activity on the customer profile bore no relation to the observed activity, which appeared to involve complex, high-value transfers with entities operating in diverse sectors.

The due diligence file lacked evidence of ongoing monitoring or periodic review. The account was assigned a medium risk rating at onboarding, which typically mandates a periodic review every eighteen to twenty-four months, depending on the specific customer segment. However, given the significant deviations from the expected activity profile and the substantial transaction volume, an event-driven review should have been triggered earlier in the relationship. The file did not contain any record of an event-driven review being initiated by the relationship manager or the compliance department prior to the commencement of this investigation. The last documented contact with the customer was a brief email exchange between the relationship manager and Thaddeus Fontaine on October 3, 2023, regarding a routine administrative matter. There was no evidence that the relationship manager sought to clarify the nature of the business activities or the source of funds for the substantial transactions flowing through the account. When the deficiencies in the due diligence file were identified during the course of this investigation, the account held a balance of $150,305.28. The combination of an uncleared documentary exception, a late-filed beneficial ownership certification, inadequate source of funds evidence, and a transaction profile that fundamentally contradicted the stated business purpose resulted in a due diligence file that could not support the assigned risk rating or provide a reasonable understanding of the customer's activities.

section_title: Prior Alert and Disposition History - Thaddeus Fontaine
body:
Prior Alert and Disposition History - Thaddeus Fontaine

A review of the automated transaction monitoring system was conducted for the relationship of Thaddeus Fontaine. This review identified that two prior alerts were generated on this customer file prior to the current escalation. Both previous alerts were closed without the filing of a Suspicious Activity Report. A retrospective analysis of these closures indicates that the dispositions may have been inadequately reasoned given the information available at the time, particularly in relation to the customer due diligence deficiencies now apparent.

The first alert generated on October 3, 2023. This alert was triggered by a scenario designed to detect rapid movement of funds following a large incoming wire transfer. The alert details indicated that the initial funding of the Thaddeus Fontaine account, a wire transfer in the amount of $872,548.20, was received on September 14, 2023. This funding originated from an account held at another domestic financial institution in the name of Summit Gate Fabrication Inc. The reviewing analyst noted that a significant portion of these funds was subsequently remitted outward between September 19, 2023, and September 27, 2023. These outgoing wire transfers were directed to Silverthorn Holdings Trading Co. and Ardent Machinery Corp.

The disposition narrative for this initial alert stated that the activity appeared consistent with the stated purpose of the account. The analyst recorded that Thaddeus Fontaine had described his business as acting as an intermediary for commercial equipment procurement. The analyst concluded that the incoming wire from Summit Gate Fabrication Inc. represented payment for equipment, and the subsequent outgoing wires to Silverthorn Holdings Trading Co. and Ardent Machinery Corp. were payments to suppliers. The alert was closed on October 11, 2023, with a determination that the rapid movement of funds was justified by the nature of the customer's declared business model.

A review of the analyst's rationale reveals significant shortcomings. The analyst relied entirely on the customer's stated occupation to explain the activity, without verifying that the occupation was actually recorded in the customer due diligence profile. Current review of the file shows that the occupation field for Thaddeus Fontaine was left blank at onboarding and remains blank. The analyst's assertion that the activity was consistent with the stated business purpose was therefore unfounded, as no business purpose had been formally established in the bank's records. Furthermore, the analyst failed to recognize that the account had been opened on a documentary exception regarding the customer's physical address, and this exception had not been cleared at the time the alert was reviewed. The failure to identify these missing foundational elements of the KYC profile undermines the conclusion that the rapid movement of a sum exceeding three-quarters of a million dollars was legitimate.

The second alert generated on October 18, 2023. This alert was triggered by a scenario designed to identify high-value wire transfers involving counterparties not previously associated with the account. The alert centered on a single outgoing wire transfer in the amount of $704,962.00, executed on October 19, 2023. This transfer was directed to an entity named Mapleford Fabrication Holdings Ltd., located in a foreign jurisdiction. The alert details noted that Mapleford Fabrication Holdings Ltd. had no prior transactional history with Thaddeus Fontaine.

The disposition narrative for this second alert indicated that the reviewing analyst contacted the relationship manager for clarification regarding the purpose of the transfer. The analyst recorded that the relationship manager stated the funds were related to a commercial real estate investment in the receiving jurisdiction. The analyst noted that Thaddeus Fontaine was involved in various investment activities and concluded that the transfer, while large, was not inconsistent with a high-net-worth individual diversifying their portfolio. The alert was closed on October 23, 2023, based on the relationship manager's explanation.

A retrospective analysis of this second closure also identifies significant flaws. The analyst accepted the relationship manager's explanation without requiring any supporting documentation to verify the source of funds or the legitimacy of the real estate investment. The sum of $704,962.00 was transferred without any evidence on file to substantiate its origin or purpose. This is particularly concerning given that the stated purpose of the transfer, a foreign real estate investment, bore no relation to the previously claimed, though undocumented, business model of commercial equipment procurement. The analyst failed to recognize the inconsistency between the activity observed in the first alert and the explanation provided for the second alert. The declared activity, as relayed by the relationship manager, bore no relation to the observed activity from the previous month. The analyst also failed to revisit the foundational KYC profile, missing the ongoing documentary exception and the missing occupation information. The reliance on undocumented assertions from the relationship manager to explain a large, out-of-pattern international transfer, in the context of an incomplete due diligence file, renders the closure rationale inadequate. The failure to identify the ongoing KYC deficiencies during the review of both alerts suggests a systemic issue in the alert disposition process for this relationship. The analysts reviewing these alerts did not adequately integrate customer due diligence information into their transactional analysis, leading to closures based on unverified assumptions rather than documented facts. The prior dispositions did not adequately mitigate the risks associated with the unverified initial funding and the subsequent large-value transfers.

Prior Filing Continuity Assessment

An assessment of the historical filing record for Lanternhill Marine Services Trading Co. indicates that the activity identified during the current review period represents a continuation of the patterns described in a prior Suspicious Activity Report filed by Cortex Bank and Trust. The preceding report covered a six-month period ending immediately prior to the commencement of the current review period on September 14, 2023. The prior filing detailed significant inconsistencies between the customer's stated business model and the transactional activity observed within account 66-51447-5. Specifically, the prior narrative noted that Lanternhill Marine Services Trading Co. was onboarded as a domestic provider of marine engine repair services, yet the account primarily received large, round-dollar incoming wire transfers from overseas counterparties, which were subsequently dissipated through numerous smaller outgoing wires to a network of domestic trading companies. The current review confirms that this fundamental pattern—the receipt of large, unexplained incoming funds and their rapid, fragmented disbursement—has persisted without interruption or substantive alteration. The rationale for determining that the current activity constitutes continuing activity rather than a novel typology rests on the consistency of this core transactional behavior, despite minor variations in the specific counterparties involved.

The prior filing focused significantly on incoming wire transfers from Obsidian Logistics Group LLC. These transfers, which occurred at irregular intervals, lacked clear commercial purpose and were inconsistent with the anticipated revenue streams for a marine engine repair business. During the current review period, beginning September 14, 2023, the volume of incoming wires from Obsidian Logistics Group LLC decreased. However, this reduction was offset by a corresponding increase in incoming wire activity from Silverthorn Holdings Trading Co. and Ardent Machinery Corp. The nature of these incoming transfers—large, round-dollar amounts originating from entities with no apparent connection to the marine services industry—remains identical to the pattern reported previously. The substitution of one set of counterparties for another, while maintaining the same underlying transactional characteristics, is indicative of a continuous operational methodology rather than a departure from the previously established pattern.

Similarly, the disbursement phase of the activity has maintained its prior characteristics. The preceding report documented the rapid transfer of funds out of account 66-51447-5 to entities such as Mapleford Fabrication Holdings Ltd. and Lakebridge Exports Inc. The current review period reveals ongoing disbursements to these same entities, alongside new outgoing transfers to Millpond Capital Holdings Ltd. The outgoing wires continue to be executed shortly after the receipt of incoming funds, often reducing the account balance to a nominal amount. The velocity of these transactions and the lack of apparent commercial logic connecting Lanternhill Marine Services Trading Co. to the recipient entities are consistent with the findings of the previous investigation. The continuity in the method of dissipation further supports the conclusion that the activity is ongoing.

The deficiencies in the Customer Due Diligence file for Lanternhill Marine Services Trading Co., which were a primary focus of the prior filing, have also persisted into the current review period. The preceding report noted that the account was opened subject to a documentary exception regarding the verification of the entity's principal place of business. This exception was never cleared. A review of the customer profile conducted during the current investigation confirms that the required documentation remains outstanding. Furthermore, the prior filing highlighted that the beneficial owner attestation was dated after the initial funding of the account, raising concerns about the adequacy of the onboarding process. The current review confirms this chronological discrepancy remains unaddressed within the customer file. The ongoing failure to rectify these fundamental KYC deficiencies, despite the passage of time and the filing of a previous Suspicious Activity Report, underscores the continuous nature of the compliance risk associated with this relationship.

The prior filing also documented that the occupation field for a key principal associated with Lanternhill Marine Services Trading Co. was left blank, a notable omission given the account's medium risk tier assignment. The current review confirms that this field remains unpopulated. The persistence of incomplete customer information, coupled with the ongoing, unexplained transactional activity, indicates that the risk profile of the relationship has not been adequately mitigated since the prior report. The aggregate activity conducted on the deficient file during the current review period, totaling $2,885,112.91, demonstrates the scale of the ongoing risk exposure. The failure to remediate the identified KYC deficiencies while facilitating significant transaction volumes is a continuous vulnerability.

While the specific counterparties involved in the transactional network have evolved slightly, the overarching typology—a due diligence file that cannot support the risk rating the account was given, combined with declared activity that bears no relation to observed activity—remains unchanged. The prior filing established that Lanternhill Marine Services Trading Co. was acting as a conduit for funds rather than operating as a legitimate marine services business. The activity observed between September 14, 2023, and August 1, 2024, reinforces this assessment. The unverified initial funding amount of $872,548.20, noted in the prior review, established a baseline of unexplained capital that has continued to circulate through the account. The largest single transaction with no source-of-funds evidence during the current period, amounting to $704,962.00, is consistent with the magnitude of unexplained transactions reported previously.

The balance held when the file deficiency was identified during the current review, which was $150,305.28, represents a snapshot of the ongoing flow of funds through an inadequately documented account. The continuity of the behavior is evidenced not merely by the repetition of specific transactions, but by the persistence of the underlying operational characteristics: the reliance on an incomplete KYC profile, the receipt of funds from anomalous sources, and the rapid disbursement to unrelated entities. The reviewing analyst determined that the minor shifts in counterparty relationships do not alter the fundamental nature of the suspicious activity. Therefore, the activity observed during the current review period is assessed as a direct continuation of the patterns detailed in the prior filing, warranting ongoing reporting under the established typology.

section_title: Customer Due Diligence File Review - Lanternhill Marine Services Trading Co.
body:
Customer Due Diligence File Review - Lanternhill Marine Services Trading Co.

During the periodic review of Lanternhill Marine Services Trading Co. account 66-51447-5, significant customer due diligence file deficiencies were identified. The account was boarded with a medium risk tier on September 14, 2023. The customer profile indicates the entity is involved in marine salvage and equipment leasing, operations typically associated with heightened AML risk. The file, however, lacks the requisite documentation to substantiate this risk classification or the volume of funds subsequently processed.

The initial funding of the account occurred on September 15, 2023, consisting of a wire transfer. The file lacks documentation verifying the source of these initial funds. The unverified initial funding amount was $872,548.20. Standard procedure dictates that source of funds documentation be collected and verified prior to or commensurate with the initial deposit, particularly for accounts exhibiting this risk profile. No such documentation was located in the file, nor was there evidence that the onboarding officer attempted to procure it.

The beneficial ownership certification on file for Lanternhill Marine Services Trading Co. was executed on September 19, 2023. This post-dates the initial funding of the account. Regulatory requirements stipulate that beneficial ownership information must be obtained prior to the commencement of account activity. The delay in securing this certification constitutes a procedural deficiency. The certification identifies Thaddeus Fontaine and Solveig Cromwell as holding significant ownership stakes, with Delia Dalrymple listed as a control person.

A review of the identification documents provided for the beneficial owners and control persons revealed further inconsistencies. The identification provided for Thaddeus Fontaine was a state-issued driver's license. The copy retained in the file was illegible in several critical areas, including the expiration date. The identification provided for Solveig Cromwell was a passport, which appeared valid. However, the occupation field on the customer profile for Solveig Cromwell was left blank. Given the medium risk tier assigned to the account and the nature of the declared business, a complete customer profile, including verifiable occupation details for all beneficial owners, is required. The file lacks evidence that the relationship manager sought to rectify this omission. The identification provided for Delia Dalrymple was current and legible.

The file indicates that the account was opened subject to a documentary exception. The specific nature of the exception was not clearly articulated in the onboarding notes. However, a review of the required documentation checklist suggests the exception pertained to the collection of the entity's articles of incorporation and a certificate of good standing. The exception was approved by the onboarding officer with the stipulation that the outstanding documents be provided within thirty days of account opening. There is no evidence in the file that these documents were ever received. The documentary exception was never cleared, yet the account remained active and unrestricted.

Subsequent to the initial funding, the account exhibited significant transactional volume. The file lacks source of wealth or source of funds corroboration for this ongoing activity. The largest single transaction with no source-of-funds evidence was $704,962.00, which posted on October 3, 2023. The declared activity on the customer profile anticipated an average monthly transactional volume in the low six-figure range, consisting primarily of equipment lease payments and salvage recovery proceeds. The observed activity, however, involved frequent, large-dollar wire transfers to and from entities whose relationship to Lanternhill Marine Services Trading Co. could not be established from the information contained in the file. The declared activity bears no relation to the observed activity. The file lacks documentation, such as invoices, contracts, or bills of lading, that would support the economic purpose of these transfers.

Counterparties involved in the observed activity included Silverthorn Holdings Trading Co., Ardent Machinery Corp., and Mapleford Fabrication Holdings Ltd. The file contains no information regarding these entities, nor does it document any effort by the bank to understand the business relationships between these counterparties and the subject entity. The lack of documented due diligence on these counterparties further diminishes the utility of the file in assessing the AML risk posed by the account.

The periodic review of the account was scheduled for September 2024, one year after onboarding, consistent with the medium risk tier assignment. However, the review was initiated early due to transaction monitoring alerts generated by the volume and velocity of the wire activity. At the time the file deficiency was identified during this review, the balance held was $150,305.28. The aggregate activity conducted on the deficient file was $2,885,112.91. The volume of funds processed through the account without adequate due diligence documentation presents a substantial AML risk.

The file review process also noted interactions with other entities, including Summit Gate Fabrication Inc., Summit Gate Trading Enterprises LLC, Lakebridge Exports Inc., Obsidian Logistics Group LLC, and Millpond Capital Holdings Ltd. The nature of these interactions was not documented in the customer profile or any subsequent file updates. The absence of this information impedes a comprehensive understanding of the customer's business network and transactional behavior. The file does not support the medium risk rating assigned; the observed activity and lack of corroborating documentation suggest a higher risk profile that warrants enhanced due diligence measures, which were not implemented. The deficiencies identified in the collection, verification, and maintenance of customer information represent a significant departure from standard BSA/AML compliance procedures.

section_title: Prior Alert and Disposition History - Summit Gate Fabrication Inc.
body:
Prior Alert and Disposition History - Summit Gate Fabrication Inc.

The relationship with Summit Gate Fabrication Inc. generated four automated monitoring alerts prior to the current review, none of which resulted in a referral for escalation or the filing of a Suspicious Activity Report. These alerts were triggered by the transaction monitoring system and assigned to tier-one analysts for review and disposition. The current investigation, prompted by a periodic high-risk customer review, indicates that the rationales applied to clear the prior alerts were insufficient and failed to address underlying customer due diligence deficiencies. The aggregate activity conducted on the deficient file totaled $2,885,112.91.

On September 19, 2023, an alert was generated for Summit Gate Fabrication Inc. under a scenario designed to detect rapid, high-value movement of funds following account opening. The alert triggered on the unverified initial funding amount of $872,548.20, received via incoming wire transfer from Mapleford Fabrication Holdings Ltd., a counterparty not listed in the initial customer profile. The assigned analyst reviewed the alert and closed it on September 27, 2023, with a disposition rationale stating that the incoming funds were consistent with the expected activity for a fabrication company receiving capital from a related holding entity. The analyst noted that the names of the two entities were similar, suggesting a corporate relationship.

The disposition rationale for the September 19, 2023 alert is now assessed as inadequate. The analyst relied on an assumption of a legitimate corporate relationship based solely on name similarity, without verifying the relationship or the source of funds. The initial customer due diligence profile for Summit Gate Fabrication Inc. lacked expected counterparties, and the receipt of significant funding from an unknown entity shortly after account opening warranted further scrutiny. Furthermore, the analyst failed to identify that the account was opened on a documentary exception that was never cleared, meaning the foundational identity and business purpose of the customer were not fully established at the time the funds were received.

On October 3, 2023, a second alert was generated for the Summit Gate Fabrication Inc. account, this time under a scenario targeting large round-dollar transfers to previously unseen counterparties. The alert was triggered by an outgoing wire transfer in the amount of $704,962.00 to Ardent Machinery Corp. The reviewing analyst closed the alert on October 11, 2023. The disposition notes stated that the transaction was reviewed and deemed consistent with a fabrication company purchasing machinery or equipment. The analyst concluded that the transaction did not appear suspicious and required no further action.

The closure of the October 3, 2023 alert represents a significant oversight. The transaction of $704,962.00 is the largest single transaction with no source-of-funds evidence in the account's history. The analyst's conclusion that the transfer was for machinery purchase was speculative and not supported by invoice documentation, contracts, or any other verifying information. The rationale failed to address the rapid depletion of the unverified initial funding and did not question the lack of a clear business rationale for the sudden, large disbursement. The analyst also did not notice that the beneficial owner attestation on file was dated after the first funding, a discrepancy that should have raised concerns about the customer onboarding process.

A third alert triggered on October 18, 2023, under a scenario designed to monitor for unusual patterns of incoming funds from multiple, unrelated sources. The alert consolidated several incoming wire transfers from Obsidian Logistics Group LLC and Silverthorn Holdings Trading Co. The analyst assigned to the alert reviewed the activity and closed the alert on October 19, 2023. The disposition stated that the incoming funds appeared to be routine business receipts for services rendered by Summit Gate Fabrication Inc. The analyst noted that the counterparties appeared to be legitimate businesses engaged in logistics and trading.

The October 19, 2023 disposition is problematic as it accepted the declared activity of the customer without verifying it against the observed transaction patterns. The customer profile indicated a fabrication business, yet the incoming funds were from logistics and trading companies, suggesting a potential mismatch between the declared business purpose and the actual use of the account. The analyst did not attempt to reconcile this discrepancy or request supporting documentation, such as invoices or bills of lading, to substantiate the nature of the business transactions. The rationale relied on surface-level assessments of counterparty names rather than a substantive review of the economic purpose of the transfers.

The final prior alert for Summit Gate Fabrication Inc. was generated on October 23, 2023, under a scenario monitoring for rapid flow-through of funds. The alert captured a series of incoming transfers from Lakebridge Exports Inc. and Millpond Capital Holdings Ltd., followed by almost immediate outgoing transfers to Summit Gate Trading Enterprises LLC. The reviewing analyst closed the alert on the same day, citing that the activity was consistent with a company managing cash flows between related entities. The analyst noted the shared name component between the subject and the receiving entity, assuming a legitimate intercompany transfer purpose.

The disposition of the October 23, 2023 alert exhibits the same analytical flaws as the previous reviews. The analyst assumed a legitimate relationship based on name similarity without any verification. The rapid flow-through of funds, coupled with the involvement of multiple counterparties across different industries (exports, capital holdings, trading), presented a complex transaction pattern that was dismissed with a generic rationale. The analyst failed to recognize that the declared activity of fabrication bore no relation to the observed activity of acting as a pass-through entity for various trading and capital firms. The cumulative effect of these prior dispositions was a failure to identify and escalate the significant customer due diligence deficiencies and the unusual transaction patterns that characterized the Summit Gate Fabrication Inc. relationship.

Transaction Analysis - Delia Dalrymple

The account established for Delia Dalrymple exhibited a transactional velocity that was misaligned with the declared anticipated activity profile recorded at onboarding. While the initial risk rating model assigned a medium risk tier to the relationship, the subsequent transaction volume and sequencing demonstrated characteristics that could not be reconciled with that assessment. The reviewing analyst noted that the account experienced rapid, high-volume cycling of funds, a pattern that is frequently observed in accounts where the primary function is the transit of capital rather than the retention of deposits for legitimate personal or business use. The aggregate activity conducted on the deficient file reached $2,885,112.91 during the review period. This figure significantly exceeded the expected transactional volume for an individual account, prompting closer scrutiny of the specific flow of funds. The initial funding of the account, which occurred shortly after opening, involved an unverified initial funding amount of $872,548.20. The source of these initial funds was not clearly documented in the onboarding materials, and subsequent requests for corroborating documentation were not fulfilled. This lack of transparency regarding the origin of the initial capital injection established a baseline of concern regarding the overall purpose of the account.

Following the initial funding, the account exhibited a pattern of receiving large incoming transfers, which were then rapidly disbursed to various external counterparties. The timing of these transactions was notable, with incoming funds frequently arriving early in the business day and being largely depleted through outgoing wire transfers before the close of the same business day. This rapid in-and-out movement of funds, often involving amounts in the high six figures, suggests a deliberate effort to minimize the duration that funds were held within Cortex Bank and Trust. The sequencing of these transactions was consistent with a pass-through methodology. For example, on September 15, 2023, the account received a significant incoming transfer. Within hours, a corresponding outgoing transfer, slightly smaller than the incoming amount, was initiated. This pattern of receiving funds and immediately transferring them out, often leaving only a nominal balance, was repeated numerous times throughout the review period. This behavior is indicative of an account functioning as an intermediary rather than a repository for stable assets. The reviewing analyst observed that the largest single transaction with no source-of-funds evidence was $704,962.00. This substantial transfer was executed without the customary supporting documentation that would typically accompany a transaction of that magnitude, particularly given the account's history of rapid fund depletion.

The transactional analysis also revealed a consistent use of specific counterparties for these rapid disbursements. Outgoing wire transfers were frequently directed to entities such as Ardent Machinery Corp. and Lakebridge Exports Inc. The relationship between Delia Dalrymple and these corporate entities was not evident from the account profile or the limited documentation provided during onboarding. The declared anticipated activity for the account did not include significant commercial transactions with heavy machinery or export companies. The volume and frequency of these transfers to corporate entities further underscored the disconnect between the declared purpose of the account and its actual usage. The reviewing analyst noted that the transaction descriptions provided on the wire transfer instructions were often vague or non-specific, providing little insight into the underlying economic rationale for the movement of funds. Descriptions such as "consulting fees" or "invoice payment" were used repeatedly, despite the lack of any documented consulting business or commercial enterprise associated with Delia Dalrymple.

Furthermore, the timing of the transactions often appeared coordinated to occur just prior to established reporting cutoffs. The reviewing analyst observed multiple instances where large outgoing wire transfers were initiated late in the afternoon, shortly before the end-of-day processing window. This timing strategy is sometimes employed to complicate the monitoring and review process, as transactions initiated near the cutoff may be processed before they can be thoroughly evaluated. The frequency of these late-day transactions, particularly when combined with the rapid depletion of incoming funds, suggests a calculated approach to fund movement. On September 27, 2023, and again on October 3, 2023, significant outgoing transfers were initiated within minutes of the daily wire cutoff time. Both transfers followed large incoming deposits that had cleared earlier the same day. This specific sequencing, characterized by same-day clearing and near-immediate disbursement near processing deadlines, is a structural feature often associated with efforts to obscure the origin and ultimate destination of funds.

The account's transactional behavior was also characterized by a lack of typical, everyday transactions that would be expected in a standard personal account. There was a notable absence of routine debit card purchases, utility payments, or ATM withdrawals. The account activity was almost entirely dominated by large-dollar wire transfers and ACH movements. This absence of typical consumer activity, coupled with the high volume of commercial-style transactions, strongly suggests that the account was not being used for its stated purpose. The reviewing analyst also noted that the account balance was frequently drawn down to a minimal amount following periods of high transactional activity. This pattern of rapid accumulation and immediate depletion is a common indicator of an account being used primarily as a conduit. When the file deficiency was eventually identified and a review initiated, the balance held was $150,305.28, representing a small fraction of the total funds that had moved through the account during the review period. The structural features of the transaction pattern—the high velocity, the rapid in-and-out sequencing, the use of corporate counterparties, the timing relative to processing cutoffs, and the absence of typical consumer activity—collectively present a profile that is inconsistent with a legitimate, medium-risk individual account. The observed activity bears no relation to the anticipated activity declared at account opening, and the customer was unable to substantiate the economic purpose of the high-volume transfers when inquiries were made.

Detailed Chronology

A review of the transaction history for Delia Dalrymple, operating through Cortex Bank and Trust account 79-60478-4, commenced with the opening of the account on September 14, 2023. At account opening, the occupation field on the customer profile was left blank. The account was assigned a medium risk rating. The customer file indicates that the account was opened on a documentary exception, pending the receipt of a secondary form of identification. No record of the required secondary identification document was found in the customer file for the duration of the review period. The initial funding of the account occurred on September 15, 2023, consisting of an incoming wire transfer in the amount of $872,548.20. The remitter of this initial funding transfer was Silverthorn Holdings Trading Co. The customer profile indicates an expected initial funding of a mid five-figure sum from a domestic personal checking account. The customer file contains a beneficial owner attestation form for Delia Dalrymple dated September 19, 2023, four days after the initial funding of the account.

Following the initial funding, the account exhibited a pattern of high-velocity funds transfers. On September 27, 2023, an outgoing wire transfer of $704,962.00 was directed to Ardent Machinery Corp. The transaction record for this outgoing transfer contained no corresponding invoice or other documentation to substantiate the purpose of the payment or the source of funds. This transaction represents the largest single transaction conducted through the account without supporting source-of-funds evidence. The declared expected activity for the account at opening consisted of bi-weekly payroll deposits and routine household expenses. The observed activity of large, commercial wire transfers bears no relation to the declared activity.

Activity continued into October 2023 with a series of incoming and outgoing transactions. On October 3, 2023, an incoming wire transfer of a low six-figure sum was received from Mapleford Fabrication Holdings Ltd. This was followed on October 11, 2023, by an outgoing wire transfer of a similar low six-figure sum to Summit Gate Trading Enterprises LLC. No documentation was identified to explain the relationship between Delia Dalrymple and either Mapleford Fabrication Holdings Ltd. or Summit Gate Trading Enterprises LLC. The reviewing analyst noted that the transaction activity appeared to be pass-through in nature, with funds received and subsequently transferred out within a short timeframe.

On October 18, 2023, a further incoming wire transfer of a mid five-figure sum was received from Lakebridge Exports Inc. The following day, October 19, 2023, an outgoing wire transfer of a slightly larger mid five-figure sum was sent to Obsidian Logistics Group LLC. The transaction record for the outgoing transfer indicated 'consulting fees' in the payment details field. No consulting agreement or invoices were found in the customer file. The customer profile, which remained blank in the occupation field, provided no context for consulting activity.

A subsequent incoming wire transfer of a high five-figure sum was received on October 23, 2023, from Millpond Capital Holdings Ltd. This transaction brought the account balance to a significant level, but the balance was quickly depleted by subsequent outgoing transfers. The aggregate activity conducted through account 79-60478-4 during the review period, encompassing all incoming and outgoing funds transfers, totaled $2,885,112.91. This aggregate volume significantly exceeds the activity expected for an account intended for routine household expenses and payroll deposits. The discrepancy between the declared activity and the observed transaction volume, coupled with the absence of a declared occupation, the uncleared documentary exception, and the late beneficial owner attestation, indicates a systemic deficiency in the due diligence file for this customer. At the time the file deficiency was identified by the reviewing analyst, the balance held in the account was $150,305.28. The volume and velocity of the funds transfers, combined with the lack of supporting documentation and the inconsistencies in the customer profile, suggest that the account was utilized for purposes other than those stated at account opening. The transactions involved multiple corporate counterparties, none of which were identified in the customer's onboarding documentation as expected trading partners or sources of income. The lack of clarity regarding the customer's occupation and the source of wealth further obscures the economic rationale for the observed transaction activity. The pattern of activity is consistent with a pass-through account utilized for commercial funds transfers by an individual whose business interests and relationships are not accurately reflected in the bank's records.

Transaction Analysis - Solveig Cromwell

A review of activity in the account of Solveig Cromwell (account 24-61625-3) identified a pattern of transactions inconsistent with the declared purpose of the account and the information captured in the customer due diligence file. The review period commenced with an unverified initial funding amount of $872,548.20 on September 14, 2023. This incoming wire transfer originated from Summit Gate Trading Enterprises LLC, a related business entity, and was received outside of customary banking hours, posting to the account shortly after the close of business. The due diligence file on record for Solveig Cromwell contained a documentary exception at account opening that had not been cleared at the time this initial funding was received.

Following the receipt of the initial funds, the account exhibited a rapid outflow of capital. On September 15, 2023, two outgoing domestic wire transfers were initiated. The first transfer, directed to Silverthorn Holdings Trading Co., occurred early in the business day, while the second transfer, directed to Ardent Machinery Corp., was executed shortly before the wire transfer cutoff time. The aggregate volume of these initial outflows represented a significant portion of the unverified funding amount. The sequencing of these transactions, with substantial funds arriving from a related entity and immediately being dispersed to seemingly unrelated corporate counterparties, suggests a potential pass-through arrangement.

The velocity of activity increased throughout the latter half of September. On September 19, 2023, the account received a series of incoming ACH credits from Lakebridge Exports Inc. These credits, while individually falling below regulatory reporting thresholds, were numerous and occurred within a short timeframe. The cumulative value of these ACH credits was substantial, yet the customer due diligence file provided no explanation for an anticipated business relationship with Lakebridge Exports Inc., nor did it identify the nature of the goods or services being exchanged.

The pattern of rapid disbursement continued following the influx of ACH credits. On September 27, 2023, a significant outgoing international wire transfer was initiated to Mapleford Fabrication Holdings Ltd. This transaction represented the largest single transaction with no source-of-funds evidence, totaling $704,962.00. The execution of this large international transfer, particularly without clear documentation regarding the underlying business rationale or the source of the funds being transferred, further highlights the deficiencies in the customer due diligence file and the disparity between anticipated and observed activity.

Activity in October 2023 continued to demonstrate characteristics inconsistent with standard consumer account usage. On October 3, 2023, the account received an incoming wire transfer from Millpond Capital Holdings Ltd. This transfer was followed on October 11, 2023, by a series of outgoing wire transfers to Obsidian Logistics Group LLC. The timing of these outgoing transfers appeared structured, with multiple transfers occurring on the same day, each falling just below the $10,000 currency transaction reporting threshold, although these were electronic transfers and not cash transactions. This structuring of electronic payments, while not triggering currency reporting requirements, suggests an attempt to obscure the total volume of funds being moved to a single counterparty.

The relationship between credits and debits throughout the review period remained tightly coupled. Incoming funds were routinely followed by outgoing transfers within a matter of days, leaving the account balance relatively low in comparison to the overall transaction volume. This high velocity of funds movement, coupled with the lack of underlying business documentation, is indicative of a conduit account used to facilitate the movement of capital rather than for typical personal banking purposes.

On October 18, 2023, the account received a large incoming wire transfer from Lanternhill Marine Services Trading Co. The following day, October 19, 2023, a corresponding outgoing wire transfer was initiated to Delia Dalrymple, a related individual. The transfer to Delia Dalrymple was executed shortly after the opening of business. The rapid turnaround of these funds, moving from a corporate entity to a personal account, raises questions regarding the economic purpose of the transactions and the potential commingling of personal and business funds.

Further analysis of the account activity revealed a consistent lack of correlation between the declared occupation in the customer due diligence file, which was left blank despite the account being assigned a medium risk tier, and the observed transaction patterns. The aggregate activity conducted on the deficient file reached $2,885,112.91 during the review period. The volume and complexity of the transactions, involving multiple corporate entities and international transfers, are not typically associated with an individual customer account lacking a documented occupational or business profile.

The account activity concluded the active phase of the review period on October 23, 2023, with a series of smaller outgoing transfers to unidentified third parties. The balance held when the file deficiency was identified stood at $150,305.28. The overall pattern of activity, characterized by large, unverified initial funding, rapid dispersal to various corporate counterparties, high transaction velocity, and a lack of documented business purpose, remains inconsistent with the information captured in the customer due diligence file and suggests the account may have been utilized for purposes other than those initially declared.

section_title: Counterparty and Beneficiary Analysis - Lanternhill Marine Services Trading Co.
body:
Counterparty and Beneficiary Analysis - Lanternhill Marine Services Trading Co.

The counterparty analysis for Lanternhill Marine Services Trading Co. focused on the flow of funds to and from external entities during the review period, seeking to reconcile observed activity against the expected behavior detailed in the customer profile. The review identified significant deviations from the expected counterparty profile, with a substantial portion of the aggregate activity conducted on the deficient file, which totaled $2,885,112.91, involving entities not previously disclosed to Cortex Bank and Trust. The commercial rationale for these transactions was not clearly established by the available documentation.

A primary concern was the unverified initial funding amount of $872,548.20, received via wire transfer on September 14, 2023. The originator of this transfer was identified as Silverthorn Holdings Trading Co. The customer profile for Lanternhill Marine Services Trading Co. indicated that its primary revenue sources would be derived from maritime logistics and equipment leasing. However, open-source research into Silverthorn Holdings Trading Co. revealed no apparent connection to the maritime industry. The entity is registered in a jurisdiction known for stringent corporate secrecy laws, and no public footprint, such as a website or business directory listing, could be located to verify its operational nature. The absence of a clear commercial relationship between Lanternhill Marine Services Trading Co. and Silverthorn Holdings Trading Co. renders the purpose of this initial funding ambiguous. The reviewing analyst noted that an account opened on a documentary exception that was never cleared compounded the difficulty of verifying the legitimacy of this initial capital injection.

Following the initial funding, the account exhibited a pattern of outbound wire transfers to various entities. A significant recipient of funds was Ardent Machinery Corp. Between September 19, 2023, and October 11, 2023, Lanternhill Marine Services Trading Co. originated several high-value wire transfers to Ardent Machinery Corp., including the largest single transaction with no source-of-funds evidence, which amounted to $704,962.00 on September 27, 2023. While the customer profile listed heavy equipment purchasing as a potential expense category, the scale and frequency of these transfers to Ardent Machinery Corp. appeared disproportionate to the stated operational scope of Lanternhill Marine Services Trading Co., which was ostensibly a newly established enterprise. Furthermore, public records searches indicated that Ardent Machinery Corp. was incorporated only shortly before these transfers commenced, raising questions about its capacity to fulfill orders of this magnitude. The rapid movement of funds from the unverified initial deposit to a newly formed entity is consistent with layering activity.

Further analysis of outbound transactions revealed transfers to Mapleford Fabrication Holdings Ltd. and Summit Gate Trading Enterprises LLC. These transfers, occurring primarily in October 2023, were described in the remittance information as payments for "consulting services" and "project management." However, the declared activity that bears no relation to observed activity is a persistent theme in this review. The customer profile did not anticipate significant expenditures for consulting or project management services. Open-source intelligence regarding Mapleford Fabrication Holdings Ltd. and Summit Gate Trading Enterprises LLC yielded limited information, with both entities appearing to be holding companies rather than operating businesses providing specialized services. The lack of discernible business operations for these counterparties undermines the commercial rationale provided for the transfers.

The review also identified a pattern of incoming funds from Lakebridge Exports Inc. and Obsidian Logistics Group LLC. These deposits, received in late September and October 2023, were characterized by the customer as revenue from equipment leasing. However, the timing of these receipts, occurring so soon after the initial funding and concurrent with the large outbound transfers for purported equipment purchases, presents a contradictory narrative. It is unclear how Lanternhill Marine Services Trading Co. could generate substantial leasing revenue before fully establishing its equipment inventory. A beneficial owner attestation dated after the first funding further complicates the timeline of the company's operational readiness. Open-source research on Lakebridge Exports Inc. and Obsidian Logistics Group LLC revealed that both entities share a registered address with Summit Gate Trading Enterprises LLC, suggesting a potential affiliation among the counterparties that was not disclosed to Cortex Bank and Trust. The circulation of funds among affiliated or seemingly related entities without a clear economic purpose is indicative of circular or wash trading.

Another counterparty of note is Millpond Capital Holdings Ltd., which received multiple wire transfers from Lanternhill Marine Services Trading Co. during the review period. The remittance details for these transfers often referenced "investment capital" or "loan repayment." The customer profile did not indicate that Lanternhill Marine Services Trading Co. would act as an investment vehicle or engage in significant lending or borrowing activities outside of traditional financial institutions. Millpond Capital Holdings Ltd. is registered in the same offshore jurisdiction as Silverthorn Holdings Trading Co. The movement of funds to an offshore holding company under the guise of investment or loan repayment, particularly when such activity is outside the expected behavioral profile, warrants heightened scrutiny.

The counterparty analysis also considered the involvement of the individual subjects associated with Lanternhill Marine Services Trading Co. While Thaddeus Fontaine, Solveig Cromwell, and Delia Dalrymple are listed as authorized signers or beneficial owners, their individual accounts at Cortex Bank and Trust did not exhibit direct transactional links to the counterparties identified in this review. However, the reviewing analyst noted that an occupation field left blank on a high-risk account for one of the beneficial owners hindered the ability to assess whether their professional background aligned with the complex international transactions conducted by Lanternhill Marine Services Trading Co. The inability to fully verify the professional profiles of the key individuals associated with the business further obscures the context of the counterparty relationships.

The aggregate activity involving these counterparties demonstrates a significant departure from the expected transactional behavior of a domestic maritime services company. The reliance on newly formed entities, offshore holding companies, and counterparties with opaque ownership structures or shared addresses suggests a concerted effort to obfuscate the true nature and purpose of the funds being transferred. The balance held when the file deficiency was identified, which was $150,305.28, represents a fraction of the total funds that flowed through the account, underscoring the rapid velocity of the transactions. The commercial rationale provided for these payments, whether for equipment purchases, consulting services, or investment capital, is not adequately supported by the available documentation or the public profiles of the counterparties involved. The activity is consistent with a shell company network utilized for the movement of funds of unknown origin.

Geographic and Jurisdictional Risk Assessment

An assessment of geographic and jurisdictional risk factors was conducted for the activity observed in the account held by Solveig Cromwell. Cortex Bank and Trust policy dictates a heightened risk rating for accounts demonstrating significant transactional volume with high-risk foreign jurisdictions or domestic regions identified as high-intensity financial crime areas. The activity observed during the review period was evaluated against these criteria. Initial due diligence documentation listed Solveig Cromwell’s primary residence in a state not designated as a high-intensity drug trafficking area or a high-intensity financial crime area. The account file did not indicate any anticipated international wire activity at the time of onboarding.

Review of the transactional history revealed a pattern of outgoing wire transfers that was inconsistent with the initial geographic risk profile. A significant portion of the outgoing funds was directed to accounts held by Silverthorn Holdings Trading Co., an entity with a registered address in a foreign jurisdiction identified by Cortex Bank and Trust as presenting an elevated risk for money laundering and sanctions evasion. While this jurisdiction is not subject to comprehensive territorial sanctions, it is flagged within the institution’s risk framework due to strategic deficiencies in its anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism regimes, as noted by international standard-setting bodies. The frequency and volume of these international wire transfers appear incongruous with the expected domestic activity profile of the customer.

Further analysis of the outgoing wire transfers identified payments to Ardent Machinery Corp. The receiving institution for these transfers was located in a different foreign jurisdiction, one recognized as a major international financial center. While this jurisdiction generally maintains robust regulatory standards, its status as a global financial hub inherently elevates the risk of exposure to complex, cross-border financial crime typologies, including trade-based money laundering and the use of shell companies to obscure beneficial ownership. The lack of documented business rationale for these international payments, coupled with the geographic location of the beneficiaries, warrants enhanced scrutiny.

In addition to the international wire activity, the review identified domestic transactions that raised geographic concerns. The account exhibited a pattern of remote deposit capture activity, with checks originating from entities located in domestic regions geographically distant from Solveig Cromwell’s stated residence. Notably, several large-dollar checks were deposited from Mapleford Fabrication Holdings Ltd., an entity located in a state thousands of miles from the customer's home branch. The distance between the customer’s location and the origin of these funds presents a geographic anomaly that requires further investigation to determine if a legitimate economic nexus exists. The reviewing analyst noted that the documentation on file was insufficient to explain the geographic dispersion of these transactions.

The geographic risk assessment also considered the location of the branches where in-person activity occurred. While the majority of the transactional volume was conducted electronically via wire transfers and remote deposit capture, limited in-branch activity was observed. This activity consisted primarily of small-dollar cash withdrawals conducted at a branch located near Solveig Cromwell’s stated residence. This in-branch activity appeared consistent with routine personal banking and did not present significant geographic risk factors. However, the volume and nature of the electronic transactions overshadowed this localized activity.

The geographic footprint of the counterparties involved in the transactions was further analyzed. The account received incoming wire transfers from Summit Gate Trading Enterprises LLC. The originator's address for these transfers was located in a state identified by law enforcement as a high-intensity financial crime area, known for elevated levels of fraud and illicit financial flows. The receipt of funds from an entity located in a high-risk domestic jurisdiction, particularly when the customer’s profile does not indicate a business relationship with entities in that region, constitutes a geographic red flag.

The review also noted transactions involving Lakebridge Exports Inc., an entity whose registered address was in a foreign jurisdiction different from those previously mentioned. This jurisdiction, while not on Cortex Bank and Trust’s highest-risk list, is recognized for offering corporate structures that prioritize opacity, such as international business companies and trusts, which can be utilized to obscure true beneficial ownership. The engagement with an entity located in a jurisdiction known for corporate secrecy adds a layer of jurisdictional complexity and risk to the account profile.

The aggregate activity conducted on the deficient file, totaling $2,885,112.91, involved counterparties spanning multiple domestic and international jurisdictions. The geographic dispersion of these counterparties, coupled with the presence of high-risk jurisdictions and the lack of a documented business rationale for this cross-border activity, presents a significant deviation from the anticipated geographic risk profile. The initial due diligence documentation failed to capture the true geographic scope of the customer's financial activities.

Furthermore, the review identified outgoing wire transfers to Obsidian Logistics Group LLC. The beneficiary address for these transfers was located in a state known for its proximity to international borders and significant volumes of cross-border trade. While legitimate business activities frequently occur in this region, it is also recognized as a transit point for illicit goods and funds. The transactions with an entity located in a border region, without corresponding documentation to substantiate the business purpose, contribute to the overall geographic risk assessment.

The transactions involving Millpond Capital Holdings Ltd. also presented jurisdictional considerations. The registered address for this entity was in a foreign jurisdiction characterized by its status as an offshore financial center. Such jurisdictions are often utilized for tax optimization and asset protection, but they also present heightened risks for money laundering due to their favorable tax regimes and strict bank secrecy laws. The flow of funds to an offshore financial center, particularly without a clear economic rationale, requires careful evaluation within the context of the geographic risk framework.

The geographic analysis highlights a substantial disconnect between the expected domestic activity profile and the observed complex, multi-jurisdictional transactional behavior. The involvement of entities located in high-risk foreign jurisdictions, high-intensity domestic financial crime areas, and offshore financial centers elevates the jurisdictional risk associated with the account. The lack of sufficient documentation to explain the economic nexus between Solveig Cromwell and these geographically diverse counterparties further compounds the geographic risk concerns. The geographic footprint of the activity observed during the review period is not supported by the information maintained in the customer's due diligence file.

Related Party Network Analysis

Review of the customer file for Solveig Cromwell identified an undocumented business relationship with Summit Gate Fabrication Inc. Cromwell is listed as a secondary signatory on the Summit Gate Fabrication Inc. account, a detail not present in her personal account file or the initial onboarding documentation for Summit Gate Fabrication Inc. The addition of Cromwell as a signatory appears to have occurred on October 3, 2023, following the initial funding of the Summit Gate Fabrication Inc. account. This undocumented connection between a personal account holder and a commercial entity, particularly one added after initial funding, represents a gap in the customer due diligence profile for both subjects.

Further analysis of the Summit Gate Fabrication Inc. account documentation revealed a shared registered agent address with Mapleford Fabrication Holdings Ltd. While shared registered agents are common in corporate formation, the combination of this shared address and subsequent transactional activity warrants further scrutiny. The customer due diligence file for Summit Gate Fabrication Inc. does not identify Mapleford Fabrication Holdings Ltd. as an affiliate, subsidiary, or anticipated counterparty. This omission is notable given the volume of subsequent transactional activity between the two entities, which appears inconsistent with the stated business purpose of Summit Gate Fabrication Inc.

Analysis of wire transfer records for the review period identified a pattern of funds transfers between Solveig Cromwell’s personal account and the Summit Gate Fabrication Inc. account. These transfers were frequently followed by outbound wires from Summit Gate Fabrication Inc. to Mapleford Fabrication Holdings Ltd. The documentation on file for Cromwell does not indicate an ownership stake or formal employment relationship with Summit Gate Fabrication Inc. that would explain this flow of funds. The lack of documented justification for these transfers, combined with the subsequent routing of funds to an entity sharing a registered agent with Summit Gate Fabrication Inc., suggests a level of coordination not captured in the initial risk assessment.

A review of the account documentation for Thaddeus Fontaine identified a shared residential address with Delia Dalrymple. Both Fontaine and Dalrymple hold personal accounts at Cortex Bank and Trust. The customer due diligence files for both individuals do not indicate any formal business relationship or shared financial interests. However, a review of transactional activity identified regular, coordinated cash deposits into both accounts. These deposits often occurred on the same day or within consecutive days, frequently at different branch locations.

Subsequent to these cash deposits, funds were routinely transferred from the accounts of Fontaine and Dalrymple to the account of Lanternhill Marine Services Trading Co. The customer due diligence file for Lanternhill Marine Services Trading Co. lists Thaddeus Fontaine as a beneficial owner. The file does not list Delia Dalrymple as an owner, officer, or anticipated counterparty. The routing of funds from Dalrymple’s personal account to an entity beneficially owned by Fontaine, with whom she shares a residential address, suggests a coordinated effort to fund the business account using multiple personal accounts. This activity was not anticipated in the onboarding documentation for any of the three accounts.

Further review of the Lanternhill Marine Services Trading Co. account identified outbound wire transfers to Silverthorn Holdings Trading Co. The customer due diligence file for Lanternhill Marine Services Trading Co. does not list Silverthorn Holdings Trading Co. as a supplier, vendor, or anticipated counterparty. The file for Lanternhill Marine Services Trading Co. describes its primary business activity as maritime logistics and freight forwarding. A review of publicly available information indicates that Silverthorn Holdings Trading Co. operates in the wholesale distribution of heavy machinery. The transactional activity between these entities appears inconsistent with the stated business purpose of Lanternhill Marine Services Trading Co.

An analysis of the counterparty network identified a shared telephone number between Silverthorn Holdings Trading Co. and Ardent Machinery Corp. The customer due diligence files for the subjects of this investigation do not contain information indicating a relationship between these two counterparties. However, wire transfer records indicate that Lanternhill Marine Services Trading Co. originated funds transfers to both Silverthorn Holdings Trading Co. and Ardent Machinery Corp. during the review period. The shared contact information between these two counterparties, combined with the fact that both received funds from Lanternhill Marine Services Trading Co., suggests a potential affiliation not disclosed during the onboarding process.

Review of the account documentation for Summit Gate Fabrication Inc. identified a beneficial owner attestation dated September 19, 2023. This date is subsequent to the unverified initial funding amount of $872,548.20 received on September 15, 2023. The receipt of significant funds prior to the completion of beneficial ownership documentation represents a material deficiency in the customer due diligence process. This deficiency is compounded by the subsequent transactional activity, which involved complex routing of funds through entities with shared contact information and undocumented affiliations.

The customer due diligence file for Summit Gate Fabrication Inc. was opened on a documentary exception that was never cleared. The nature of the exception was not clearly documented in the file. The account was assigned a medium risk tier at onboarding. Given the unverified initial funding, the delayed beneficial ownership attestation, and the complex network of undocumented affiliations identified during this review, the assigned risk tier appears inadequately supported by the information contained within the customer file. The aggregate activity conducted on the deficient file during the review period totaled $2,885,112.91. The largest single transaction with no source-of-funds evidence was an incoming wire transfer of $704,962.00.

Analysis of transactional data identified funds transfers from Summit Gate Fabrication Inc. to Summit Gate Trading Enterprises LLC. The similarity in naming conventions suggests a potential affiliation. However, the customer due diligence file for Summit Gate Fabrication Inc. does not identify Summit Gate Trading Enterprises LLC as an affiliate, subsidiary, or anticipated counterparty. Public records searches did not readily identify common ownership between the two entities. The lack of documented information regarding the relationship between these entities, combined with the volume of transactional activity, highlights a further gap in the customer profile.

A review of outbound wire transfers from Summit Gate Trading Enterprises LLC identified funds routed to Lakebridge Exports Inc. and Obsidian Logistics Group LLC. The customer due diligence files for the subjects of this investigation do not contain information regarding these entities. The routing of funds through multiple entities, some with similar naming conventions and others with undocumented affiliations, obscures the ultimate destination and purpose of the funds. This complex network of transactions, involving entities not identified in the initial risk assessment, is inconsistent with the anticipated activity documented in the customer files.

Further analysis identified wire transfers from Lanternhill Marine Services Trading Co. to Millpond Capital Holdings Ltd. The customer due diligence file for Lanternhill Marine Services Trading Co. does not list Millpond Capital Holdings Ltd. as an anticipated counterparty. Public records searches indicate that Millpond Capital Holdings Ltd. is an investment holding company. The transfer of funds from a maritime logistics company to an investment holding company does not align with the stated business purpose of Lanternhill Marine Services Trading Co. This discrepancy, along with the other undocumented affiliations and coordinated activities identified within the network, further demonstrates the inadequacy of the customer due diligence files in supporting the assigned risk ratings and understanding the true nature of the customers' activities.

section_title: Counterparty and Beneficiary Analysis - Delia Dalrymple
body:
Counterparty and Beneficiary Analysis - Delia Dalrymple

The review of counterparties associated with Delia Dalrymple, account 79-60478-4, focused on the entities sending and receiving funds, the documented rationale for these transactions, and the alignment of this activity with the expected behavior of the account. Account 79-60478-4 was established on September 15, 2023, following the initial funding of an unverified sum. The review period, extending from September 14, 2023, through August 1, 2024, captured significant transactional volume that deviated from the activity anticipated at account opening. The declared activity on the account profile, primarily consisting of low-value, domestic transfers consistent with typical retail banking use, bore no relation to the observed activity, which was characterized by high-value, complex, and international transactions. This discrepancy, combined with the presence of multiple unverified documentary exceptions, elevated the risk profile of the account, despite its initial categorization as a medium-risk account. The aggregate activity conducted on the deficient file during the review period amounted to $2,885,112.91.

A significant counterparty identified during the review was Silverthorn Holdings Trading Co. Transfers originating from account 79-60478-4 were frequently directed to this entity. Internal records indicated that Silverthorn Holdings Trading Co. maintained no existing relationship with Cortex Bank and Trust. Open-source intelligence searches revealed that Silverthorn Holdings Trading Co. is a privately held company registered in a jurisdiction known for limited corporate transparency. The business purpose of Silverthorn Holdings Trading Co. was described vaguely in available registries as "general trading and investment." The commercial rationale provided by Delia Dalrymple for the payments to Silverthorn Holdings Trading Co. was cited as "consulting services." However, the account holder was unable to substantiate this claim with supporting documentation, such as invoices, contracts, or detailed descriptions of the services rendered. The volume and frequency of these transfers, coupled with the lack of verifiable information regarding the beneficiary, raised concerns regarding the legitimacy of the transactions and their potential connection to undisclosed commercial activities or capital flight.

Another notable counterparty was Ardent Machinery Corp. Transactions involving this entity were primarily incoming, with funds being credited to account 79-60478-4. Ardent Machinery Corp. was identified through public records as a manufacturer of industrial equipment, headquartered in a high-risk jurisdiction. The rationale provided for these incoming funds was "repayment of a personal loan." This explanation appeared incongruous with the nature of the counterparty, a corporate entity engaged in heavy machinery manufacturing. The reviewing analyst requested documentation to support the loan agreement, but Delia Dalrymple failed to provide any formal agreements, repayment schedules, or evidence of the initial loan disbursement. The largest single transaction with no source-of-funds evidence, amounting to $704,962.00, was received from Ardent Machinery Corp. on October 3, 2023. The absence of corroborating evidence, combined with the significant value of the transaction and the high-risk location of the originator, suggested that the stated rationale was potentially fabricated to obscure the true nature of the funds.

Mapleford Fabrication Holdings Ltd. emerged as a frequent beneficiary of outgoing transfers from account 79-60478-4. Similar to Silverthorn Holdings Trading Co., Mapleford Fabrication Holdings Ltd. was not a customer of Cortex Bank and Trust. Publicly available information indicated that the company was a holding entity with interests in the fabrication sector. The account holder described the payments to Mapleford Fabrication Holdings Ltd. as "investments in fabrication projects." The reviewing analyst noted that the account profile for Delia Dalrymple left the occupation field blank, which is particularly concerning for a high-risk account engaging in substantial investment activities. The lack of documented expertise or professional background in the fabrication industry made the purported investments appear suspect. Furthermore, the account holder was unable to provide any prospectuses, investment agreements, or evidence of returns on these investments. The pattern of consistent, high-value transfers to Mapleford Fabrication Holdings Ltd. without adequate documentation or a clear business rationale was indicative of potential layering activity.

Transactions involving Summit Gate Trading Enterprises LLC were also scrutinized. This entity was both a sender and receiver of funds in relation to account 79-60478-4.
